title: Loops over La Silla
caption: The Milky Way and Barnard's Loop over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The central plane of our galaxy curves gently across this photograph from ESO's La Silla Observatory, dotted with bright patches of gas and threaded with dark, winding lanes of dust. At first it is a little hard to pick out against the busy background, but the constellation of Orion, the Hunter, sits at the top left.

Several pink clouds appear to spread beyond the band of the Milky Way. Their faint glow comes from ionised hydrogen gas, a sign that hot, young stars are nearby. One of them is Barnard's Loop, which wraps around the famous Orion Nebula and can be traced curving around Orion's Belt.
Beneath this colourful sky sits the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope. It has been used to chase the aftermath of gamma-ray bursts, which are among the most energetic explosions in the Universe.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, which is why faint pink hydrogen clouds such as Barnard's Loop show up at all. They are hard or impossible to see unaided.

explore: The same telescope carries the Wide Field Imager (WFI), a camera it uses to take pictures of the nearby cosmos. The photograph was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky, who captured the sky above La Silla in rich detail.
alt: The curved band of the Milky Way with bright gas patches and dark dust lanes, faint pink clouds around it, above a telescope at night.
